newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends sharply lower, Dec support intact.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends sharply lower, Dec support intact.

text.p: NYCE cotton settled lower amid brisk fund selling, but the December contract held above key support ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's weekly crop progress report.
Market sources expect the report, released at 1600 EDT, to reflect an improvement in the crop following several days of warmer temperatures throughout the Delta and the Southeast.

Trade buying supported the December contract over support at 75.00 cents. The contract closed 0.40 lower at 75.28 cents per lb, having traded from 75.80 to 74.97 cents. July ended down 0.61 at 72.09 cents, and the rest of the board finished 0.40 to 0.15 cent weaker.
Tuesday is the first notice day for July cotton.
Open interest in the July contract stood at 8,242 lots as of early Monday, down 3,633 lots from the previous session.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 25,000 lots, compared with Friday's official 13,791 lots.
